findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId with empty data likely does not bump updatedAt
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to refresh `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Prisma's `@updatedAt` is only applied when the update has fields to write. With `data: {}`, `updateMany` is effectively a no-op, so the timestamp is not refreshed. Either way it adds an extra DB round-trip on every webhook-triggered cache refresh. The PR description also says this value isn't consumed by the frontend. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly, or remove the call.

findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, which the disconnect mutation does. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`, `onChanged` is often undefined, and the query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. As a result, after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing the old "Cache Status / Last updated" entry and the delete action until a full reload. Users are told it succeeded while the UI still shows cached data.

findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential isn't found or isn't owned by the user, the handler throws a generic `Error`. tRPC reports this as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), and the error gets logged/alerted as a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) so clients get a proper status and monitoring isn't polluted.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired entries
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credential without filtering on `expiresAt >= now`. Expired rows are never served by `getCachedAvailability`, yet they still make the UI report a cache with a "Last updated" timestamp. This is misleading about whether cached data is actually in use. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the where clause.

findings.title: Backfill sets all legacy rows' updatedAt to migration time
findings.body: The column is added with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so every existing cache row gets the migration timestamp as its `updatedAt`. Until each row is rewritten, the new UI will show a fresh "Last updated" time for potentially very stale cache. A more accurate backfill, e.g. `expiresAt - interval '30 days'` (the caching TTL), would avoid misleading users.

findings.title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, ignoring the user's locale from `useLocale` and their time format preference. Non-US users will see M/D/YY dates, which is ambiguous next to otherwise translated strings.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to select these fields. Any other caller of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`, such as the platform API through the legacy export, will hit type errors if its user object doesn't select them. Nothing in this PR uses these fields, so the type widening appears unnecessary.

findings.title: Script uses BSD-only sed syntax and cwd-relative paths
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E` is macOS/BSD syntax. On GNU sed (Linux), `''` is treated as the script argument and the command fails, so the env file isn't updated. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved against the current working directory rather than the script's location, so running it from the repo root writes outside the repo. Also, `cleanup` always exits 0, even on the rate-limit and failed-to-extract-URL paths, so callers can't detect these failures.
